tagline: Costa Rica's quiet wellness capital hides behind a wall of jungle — no buildings on the beach, world-class yoga, gentle surf at Guiones and mass turtle arrivals at Ostional.
overview: Nosara stayed small on purpose. An early 1970s beach community, the 'Nosara Project', set aside jungle corridors instead of oceanfront lots, so today the beaches of Guiones and Pelada are backed by trees, not towers. The result is one of the calmest beach towns in Costa Rica.

Playa Guiones runs for nearly 7 kilometres with a forgiving, consistent beach break that surf schools love. The town is one of Latin America's biggest yoga destinations — institutes like the Nosara Yoga Institute made it famous, and open-air shalas host retreats year-round.

Just north, the black-sand Ostional refuge hosts arribadas — mass nestings when tens of thousands of olive ridley turtles storm the beach at once, one of nature's great spectacles. Add the SIBU wildlife sanctuary, Pelada's blowhole and trails through the Blue Zone forest, and Nosara earns its reputation as the peninsula's peaceful soul.

funFacts.title: A BLUE ZONE
funFacts.text: Nosara sits inside the Nicoya Blue Zone, where residents famously outlive the rest of the world.

funFacts.title: JUNGLE INSTEAD OF HOTELS
funFacts.text: Beachfront lots were never built on — a 1970s plan left the shoreline wild.

funFacts.title: THE ARRIBADA
funFacts.text: Ostional's mass turtle nestings can bring over 100,000 olive ridley turtles ashore in a few days.

funFacts.title: A BLOWHOLE BEACH

funFacts.title: ITS OWN AIRPORT
